sentences.text: Talking about my mother for forty minutes when I'd come in to talk about the mornings. Fragile isn't the word; scraped clean is closer to how the drive home felt. What do you do with your face in a waiting room where everyone knows why everyone else is there? Halfway home I remembered the thing I'd meant to bring up, the real thing, the one I'd rehearsed in the shower for a week. There's a question on the paperwork that asks you to rate your hopelessness from one to ten, like it's spice level at a restaurant. For years I'd imagined therapy as a confession booth; it turned out to be more like slowly unpacking boxes in a room with good light. I kept staring at the box of tissues on her side table, daring myself not to need it. Three weeks until the next opening, the coordinator said, and I laughed a little, because what else. She asked what brought me in, and I heard myself say "nothing, really," which we both knew was a lie. My copay was thirty dollars; my silence, apparently, has been free for years. Out in the waiting room a white-noise machine hummed by the door, so nobody could hear what the rest of us were carrying. When I finally said the ugly thing out loud, she didn't flinch, and her not flinching undid something in me. Have I ever told anyone before, he asked, and the honest answer — no one, not once — just hung there. The parking meter outside her office only took quarters, and I sat there feeding it like the hour hadn't already cost me enough. Maybe I'll cancel, maybe I'll go; either way the appointment card keeps riding around in my coat pocket. Filling out the intake form took longer than the crying did. It took forty years to walk through that door, and now she wants me back on Thursday like it's nothing. Did I actually say anything true in there, or just the version of me that performs okay? Will Thursday's update hold, or is the author still buried in revisions on the aftermath chapter? Tagged it "Heavy Themes" and "Mind the Warnings" because the last arc broke readers who skimmed. I want to write a suicide letter.
